newsitem.title: USA: Puerto Rico muni bond outlook stable -- A.G. Edwards.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rico muni bond outlook stable -- A.G. Edwards.

text.p: The rating outlook for Puerto Rico bonds remains stable despite concerns about the phase-out of federal tax incentives and the potential impact of statehood, according to a report by A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc.

"We believe the general obligation debt and other commonwealth-guaranteed debt of Puerto Rico, including debt of the Public Building Authority and Aqueduct and Sewer Authority Series 1995 bonds, are fairly rated and continue to remain a stable rating outlook," the report by fixed-income reseracher Brad Bode said.

The island's economy, especially its manufacturing base, has benefitted from federal tax law that exempted U.S. corporations from federal taxes on earnings from Puerto Rican operations and certain investments on the island.
The report said the tax breaks, contained in Section 936 of the IRS code, were "largely responsible for the significant economic growth on the island over the last 20 years."
Recent legislation will phase out the tax breaks by 2006, which could considerably slow the island's manufacturing sector and hurt new business development, the report said.
However, it said, "We continue to believe the commonwealth has ample time to find other sources of economic growth."
The cost of relocation would discourage companies from leaving, as would U.S. wage scales, which are higher on the mainland than in Puerto Rico, the report stated.
"We have not seen, nor do we expect to see, a mass exodus of companies due to the eventual elimination of the tax benefits," A.G. Edwards said.
Puerto Rico bonds enjoy exemption from federal, state and local income taxes in all 50 states, an attraction that could end if the island becomes the 51st state, the report said.
It said pro-statehood proponents were overwhelmingly re-elected last November, making another plebescite on statehood likely.
However, the report said, "Interest on Puerto Rico bonds issued prior to statehood would most likely remain tax exempt."
It said Puerto Rico's bond ratings gained stability from the island's broadening economy, record low unemployment and record high tourism activity.

Additionally, "Since 1993, a new administration has fostered greater financial control and oversight, including the instutition of several reserve funds, which should provide greater financial flexibility in the future," it said.

But the report said a higher bond rating was precluded by "significant future financial concerns" that included serious infrastructure needs, a large unfunded pension liability and plans to privatize its public health care system.
Puerto Rico's general obligation debt is rated Baa1 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and single-A by Standard & Poor's Corp.
